title: Esther 3
paragraphs: ¹ Some time later, King Ahasuerus honored Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, elevating him and giving him a seat of honor above all the other officials. ² All the royal officials at the king's gate would kneel down and bow to Haman, for the king had commanded this — but Mordecai refused to kneel or bow. ³ The other royal officials at the gate asked him, "Why do you disobey the king's command?" ⁴ Day after day they spoke to him, but he refused to listen, so they reported it to Haman to see whether Mordecai would get away with it — since he had told them he was a Jew. ⁵ When Haman saw for himself that Mordecai would not kneel or bow to him, he was filled with rage.

⁶ But killing Mordecai alone was not enough for him — he had learned what people Mordecai belonged to, and he decided to destroy all the Jews throughout the entire kingdom of Ahasuerus. ⁷ In the first month, the month of Nisan, in the twelfth year of King Ahasuerus, they cast Pur — that is, the lot — before Haman, day after day and month after month, and it fell on the twelfth month, the month of Adar. ⁸ Then Haman said to King Ahasuerus, "There is a certain people scattered throughout the provinces of your kingdom who keep themselves separate. Their customs are different from those of every other people, and they do not obey the king's laws. It is not in the king's interest to tolerate them. ⁹ If it pleases the king, let a decree be issued to destroy them. I will deposit ten thousand talents of silver into the royal treasury to pay the men who carry out this business." ¹⁰ The king took his signet ring from his finger and gave it to Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of the Jews.

¹¹ "Keep the money," the king told Haman, "and do what you want with these people." ¹² On the thirteenth day of the first month, the royal scribes were summoned and wrote out in Haman's exact words the order to the king's satraps, governors, and officials throughout every province — each province in its own script, each people in their own language. It was written in the name of King Ahasuerus and sealed with his signet ring. ¹³ Couriers carried the dispatches to every corner of the empire, ordering all people to destroy, kill, and annihilate all Jews — young and old, women and children — on a single day, the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar, and to plunder their goods. ¹⁴ A copy of the edict was to be issued as law in every province and posted publicly so all the people could be ready for that day. ¹⁵ The couriers raced out under the king's orders, and the decree was also posted in Shushan the palace. The king and Haman sat down to drink, but the city of Shushan was thrown into confusion.
